title: SymSpectra: Symmetric Information Bottleneck Framework for Molecular Structure Recognition under Imbalanced Settings
claim: Class frequency is severely skewed, rare classes are recognized worse, and the classes are strongly interdependent, so imbalance and co-occurrence must be handled.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: radial bar chart, grouped bars with significance stars, network graph
description: Three panels (a)-(c) motivate the problem. Panel (a) is a circular radial bar chart of functional-group frequencies. Each group is a labeled spoke. Spokes are colored by tier: dark blue for High, cyan for Medium, green for Low, with a legend at lower right. Spoke lengths fade toward the center. Panel (b) is a grouped bar chart of average recall for XGBoost, 1D-CNN and Transformer across Low, Medium and High frequency tiers. Teal, pale mint and orange bars carry significance brackets with p-values and asterisks. Recall rises from about 0.65–0.74 on Low to about 0.9 on High. Panel (c) is a network graph of blue nodes for functional groups, with thin edges and a dense central cluster of common groups such as Amine, Alkane and Ether. Sparse outliers such as Enamine and Imide sit at the periphery, which shows the dependencies between groups.
caption: (a) Distribution of functional groups derived from the Alberts et al. dataset, categorized into three tiers to highlight class
abstract: Identifying molecular structures from spectral data is essential for early-stage chemical analysis, yet it remains a difficult task due to severe functional group imbalance and complex inter-group dependencies, which often cause existing methods to overfit frequent groups while underperforming on rare ones. To address these issues, we present SymSpectra , a Sym metric Conditional Information Bottleneck (SCIB) framework designed to seamlessly integrate multi-modal Spectra features. Our model employs the SCIB framework to fuse multi-modal spectroscopic data into a unified representation, effectively preserving discriminative signals while mitigating redundancy. To enhance robustness against data imbalance, we incorporate conditional mutual information into the training objective, increasing the model’s sensitivity to rare functional groups and challenging molecular cases. Additionally, a specialized module captures the dependencies among functional groups, improving both prediction accuracy and chemically meaningful interpretability. Experiments on multimodal spectral datasets show that SymSpectra outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an F1-score of 0.970 in substructure classification and demonstrating strong robustness under various imbalance settings.
